answer: Each day the watcher notes which seracs stand and which have fallen, timing every collapse to the minute in the watch record. A juniper collapse invented at a desk fails the record: at the mirror of the fall the ice must have crashed exactly as the watcher heard it, and an invented fall is too quiet. Faking a season of watches means living at the station for five months, bribing a watcher and paying 19,800, while the vertex file in the observatory is read at every inspection, so a serac whose fall was never watched is thrown out.
